headline: Van der Voort says 48-player Grand Slam format has lost its edge
standfirst: The former PDC player prefers the old groups of four and says three-man groups have drained the drama from the opening stage.
body: Vincent van der Voort has criticised the PDC's expanded Grand Slam of Darts, saying the move to a 48-player field has cost the event part of its identity.
The tournament grew from 32 players to 48 this year, with 16 groups of three rather than eight groups of four. Only the group winner reaches the last 16.

Speaking on the Darts Draait Door podcast, the former professional said he preferred the old system. "I didn't like it that much," he said, adding that it is also better for sponsors and fans, who see players more often. Under the new format, he noted, players competed on Saturday and then did not return until Tuesday.

Van der Voort argued that the old groups produced more tension on the final night, when players could still progress or go out through several scenarios, with legs won and lost also coming into play. In his view that uncertainty is largely gone.

He is not against knockout darts, but feels the Grand Slam was known for its group stage. His preference would have been two group stages with 32 players, with the 16 survivors drawn into new groups before the quarter-finals, semi-finals and final.
He does not expect the PDC to adopt that idea. The last-16 ties begin on Thursday.
